verdict.rationale: First-party material documents support for Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD and Kubernetes, for architectures from x86/amd64 through ARM, RISC-V 64 and PowerPC, and for SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB and MS SQL. Low-resource operation is documented (a Raspberry Pi 3 suffices for small workloads) and corroborated hands-on by users on a $5 VPS, 4GB RAM and an Atom x7 fitlet2. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the multiple database backends and of non-x86 architecture and OS deployments.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can run a self-hosted instance on low-resource hardware across multiple OSes, CPU architectures, and database backends

citations.quote: it works across all the platforms and architectures that are supported by Go, including Linux, macOS, FreeBSD/OpenBSD and Windows on x86, amd64, ARM, RISC-V 64 and PowerPC
Offers seamless integration with leading databases, including SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB, and MS SQL.
A Raspberry Pi 3 is powerful enough to run Gitea for small workloads.
Gitea performs well even on slow hardware (a fitlet2 with an Atom x7-E3950 and 16GB RAM), whereas GitLab, which they use at work, doesn't.
Free, self-hosted Git service under the MIT license.
